chung.Learning-Teaching Method:
- Offline/Online learning.
- Project-Based Learning (PBL): An Integrated Export–Import Transaction Project is developed through staged milestones from opportunity identification to transaction completion, document-pack preparation, presentation, and individual defence.
- Research-Based Learning (RBL): Students investigate product–market–partner opportunities, market-access conditions, buyer/supplier credibility, regulatory requirements, logistics options, and transaction risks using evidence from the textbook, official sources, and lecturer-approved datasets.
- Applied learning methods include mini-lectures, transaction mapping, case analysis, numerical workshops, contract drafting, document-pack laboratories, simulations, peer review, project clinics, and professional defence.
chung.Time Allocation: Study hour (150h) = 45h (60 sessions) contact hours + 1h final exam + 104h self-study
chung.Description:
This course develops the applied knowledge and professional decision-making skills required to plan, execute, control, and evaluate international export–import transactions. The course follows an end-to-end transaction logic covering international trade conditions; product, market, buyer, supplier, and channel research; export pricing and import landed cost; Incoterms® 2020; international sales and channel agreements; transportation, freight forwarding, cargo insurance and claims; trade documents; foreign-exchange exposure; international payment and trade finance; export–import compliance; import regulations; customs entry, HS classification, customs valuation, rules of origin, tariffs and taxes; trade remedies; intellectual-property protection; and digital trade.

The course integrates Project-Based Learning and Research-Based Learning through an Integrated Export–Import Transaction Project. Students progressively transform research evidence into a commercially and operationally coherent transaction plan, including costing, quotation, contract, logistics, insurance, payment, compliance, customs, and document-pack outputs. The course emphasizes evidence-based reasoning, cross-document consistency, risk control, ethical conduct, and the ability to present and defend professional decisions.
chung.StudentTasks:
- Attend at least 80% of contact slots to be eligible for the final examination.
- Prepare assigned textbook sections, official references, cases, and worksheets before class.
- Participate actively in discussion, calculation workshops, contract and document laboratories, simulations, peer review, and project clinics.
- Complete three progress tests, all required individual/in-class tasks, and the Integrated Group Project according to the announced deadlines.
- Maintain a traceable record of research evidence, assumptions, calculations, sources, project contributions, and document revisions.
- Present and individually defend the group's transaction decisions and submitted evidence in Slots 19–20.
- Comply with academic integrity, professional conduct, source-verification, and AI-disclosure requirements.
chung.Tools: Internet; institutional LMS/FLM/Edunext; presentation software; spreadsheet software; word-processing software; official trade, customs, tariff, logistics, and legal databases; document templates; AI-supported learning tools as directed by the lecturer
chung.Note:
AI Policy: Generative AI and other digital tools may be used only as guided by the lecturer for idea generation, research planning, language refinement, document checking, scenario exploration, and learning support. Students must disclose AI use in assessed coursework, verify outputs against the textbook and authoritative sources, and remain fully responsible for accuracy, legality, originality, confidentiality, and professional judgment. AI use is not permitted in progress tests or the final examination unless explicitly authorized.

PBL/RBL evidence and learning products: transaction brief; research evidence matrix; buyer/supplier due-diligence scorecard; channel or sourcing rationale; export-costing/import-landed-cost worksheet; formal quotation or pro forma invoice; Incoterms decision note; draft international sales/purchase contract; logistics and cargo-insurance plan; payment and trade-finance flow; customs and compliance checklist; document pack; risk register; incident-response memorandum; presentation; and individual defence.

Central project inquiry: How can an exporter or importer design and execute a commercially viable, documentarily consistent, legally compliant, and risk-controlled international transaction for a selected product, partner, and market?

ITU coding used in the Schedule: I = Introduce; T = Teach/Practice; U = Utilize/Integrate.

clo: Analyze the international trade environment, trade agreements, market conditions, and product–market–partner information to identify and justify feasible export or import opportunities.
Calculate export prices and import landed costs, prepare commercial quotations, and select and justify appropriate Incoterms® 2020 rules and named places or ports for international transactions.

Draft and evaluate international sales or purchase contracts and selected channel agreements by applying relevant commercial principles, CISG fundamentals, and appropriate allocation of obligations, costs, risks, and remedies.
Design and evaluate transportation, freight-forwarding, cargo-insurance, and claims arrangements appropriate to the goods, route, delivery terms, and transaction risks.
Prepare and audit core export–import documents for accuracy, completeness, and consistency across contract, quotation, shipment, insurance, payment, and customs requirements.

Select and justify international payment, foreign-exchange risk-management, and trade-finance instruments, and identify documentary-credit discrepancies, fraud risks, and appropriate control measures.

Analyze and apply export–import compliance and customs requirements, including trade controls, HS classification, customs valuation, origin, tariffs and taxes, trade remedies, intellectual-property protection, and digital-trade requirements.

Develop, present, and defend an evidence-based, end-to-end export or import transaction project while demonstrating research capability, critical thinking, teamwork, professional communication, ethical judgment, and responsible use of digital and AI tools.

UNIT 1. INTERNATIONAL TRADE ENVIRONMENT AND TRANSACTION OVERVIEW
1.1 Course orientation and the end-to-end export–import transaction
- Parties, goods, information, documents, money, risk, and regulatory flows
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Introduction and transaction-related overview; IEI301 Integrated Transaction Project Brief and milestone worksheets
Before class: review the syllabus and project overview. In class: map an international transaction from inquiry to completion. After class: submit an individual transaction-flow reflection.

1.2 Growth, direction, drivers, and disruption of international trade
- Trade patterns, competitiveness, supply-chain change, and business implications
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Unit source—Textbook Chapters 1–2; lecturer-provided trade-data extract
Before class: read the assigned trade overview. In class: interpret a small trade dataset. After class: write three evidence-based implications for an exporter or importer.

1.3 WTO, regional trade agreements, MFN treatment, preferential access, and project launch
- Market-access logic and researchable transaction questions
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapters 1–2; IEI301 Integrated Transaction Project Brief and milestone worksheets; VNTR/WTO extracts

Before class: examine one trade agreement or tariff-preference example. In class: distinguish MFN and preferential treatment and formulate the group project inquiry. After class: submit the proposed product–country–transaction scope.

UNIT 2. PRODUCT, MARKET, PARTNER, AND CHANNEL RESEARCH
2.1 Export/import readiness and transaction definition
- Organizational capacity, objectives, resources, and compliance readiness
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapters 3–4 and 17; IEI301 Integrated Transaction Project Brief and milestone worksheets
Before class: review an exporter/importer profile. In class: conduct a readiness audit. After class: complete the company-and-transaction brief.

2.2 Product–market opportunity screening and research design
- Demand, competition, product adaptation, barriers, and evidence quality
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapters 4 and 17; market-screening worksheet
Before class: identify three candidate markets/products. In class: build a weighted screening matrix. After class: document indicators, sources, assumptions, and limitations.

2.3 Market access, trade data, and regulatory research
- Tariffs, non-tariff measures, permits, standards, labelling, and research traceability
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapters 2, 4, 16–18; VNTR and official-source worksheet
Before class: locate official tariff and regulatory information for the selected product. In class: build a market-access evidence matrix. After class: verify and cite each requirement.

2.4 Buyer, importer, exporter, and supplier identification and due diligence
- Credibility, capacity, commercial fit, sanctions, and transaction red flags
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapters 4, 5, 15 and 17; due-diligence scorecard
Before class: collect evidence on one potential partner. In class: apply a due-diligence scorecard. After class: record unresolved risks and required verification.

2.5 Reactive and proactive import-product selection; international supplier evaluation
- Quality, service, price, lead time, financial capability, and sourcing risk
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 17; supplier-evaluation worksheet
Before class: compare reactive and proactive sourcing. In class: evaluate sample suppliers. After class: prepare a supplier shortlist with justification.

2.6 Export channels and import sourcing arrangements
- Direct/indirect export, agent, distributor, representative, contract manufacturing, and outsourcing
- Project Milestone 1 clinic
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapters 5 and 17; Appendices N–O; IEI301 Integrated Transaction Project Brief and milestone worksheets
Before class: identify feasible channel/sourcing options. In class: compare structures and authority, margin, inventory, and control implications. After class: submit Milestone 1.

UNIT 3. EXPORT–IMPORT COSTING, QUOTATION, AND INCOTERMS® 2020
3.1 Export cost structure and determinants of international price
- Cost base, margin, competition, demand, exchange rates, and pricing objectives
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 7; costing worksheet
Before class: review cost components. In class: classify direct, indirect, transaction, and market costs. After class: construct a preliminary export-cost sheet.

3.2 Import landed cost, price escalation, channel margins, and competitiveness
- From supplier price to final market price
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapters 7 and 17; Tables 7.1–7.2 and 17.4; landed-cost worksheet
Before class: review the landed-cost example. In class: calculate total landed cost and price escalation. After class: test the project's commercial viability under two scenarios.

3.3 Progress Test 1 and applied debrief
- Scope: Units 1–2 and foundational costing concepts
Assigned materials from Sessions 1–11; review guide
Complete the individual closed-book Progress Test 1. After the test: record misconceptions and one corrective learning action.

3.4 Incoterms® 2020: purpose, scope, structure, and limitations
- Delivery, cost, risk, transport, insurance, and customs responsibilities
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 7; ICC Incoterms® 2020 reference
Before class: review the 11 rules. In class: separate delivery/risk from title/payment. After class: complete an Incoterms scope-and-limitations check.

3.5 Rules for any mode of transport
- EXW, FCA, CPT, CIP, DAP, DPU, and DDP; named place and multimodal/container decisions
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 7; Incoterms decision worksheet
Before class: compare any-mode rules. In class: solve delivery/risk/cost cases. After class: justify the rule and exact named place for the project.

3.6 Rules for sea and inland waterway transport; formal quotation workshop
- FAS, FOB, CFR, and CIF; containerization; quotation validity and assumptions
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 7; Appendix P formal quote; quotation worksheet
Before class: review sea rules and quotation fields. In class: prepare and peer-audit a formal quotation. After class: submit costing, Incoterms decision note, and revised quotation.

UNIT 4. INTERNATIONAL SALES CONTRACTS AND CHANNEL AGREEMENTS
4.1 CISG fundamentals and contract formation
- Scope, offer, acceptance, counteroffer, oral/written terms, and battle of forms
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 8; CISG official text
Before class: read the assigned CISG overview. In class: identify offer, acceptance, and counteroffer in email sequences. After class: prepare a contract-formation note.

4.2 Core commercial clauses
- Goods, specifications, quantity/tolerance, price/currency, delivery, shipment, payment, inspection, and documentary requirements
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 8; Appendix M; clause-drafting worksheet
Before class: review the contract template. In class: draft assigned clauses. After class: test each clause for clarity, measurability, and alignment with the quotation.
4.3 Performance, remedies, force majeure, warranties, liability, governing law, and dispute settlement
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 8; Appendix M; selected closing cases
Before class: identify risk-allocation clauses. In class: analyze breach and remedy scenarios. After class: revise the project's risk and dispute clauses.

4.4 Export sales/purchase contract drafting laboratory
- Integrated drafting from inquiry and quotation to contract
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 8; Appendix M; IEI301 Integrated Transaction Project Brief and milestone worksheets
Before class: bring the approved quotation and transaction facts. In class: draft the contract. After class: complete a cross-reference check against costing, Incoterms, and payment assumptions.

4.5 Distributorship agreement
- Territory, exclusivity, minimum purchases, pricing, IP, warranty, obligations, termination, and force majeure
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 5 and Appendix N
Before class: review Appendix N. In class: audit a distributorship agreement. After class: recommend whether the project should use a distributor and specify safeguards.

4.6 Sales representative agreement and channel-agreement comparison
- Authority, commission, confidentiality, customer ownership, and post-termination obligations
- Project Milestone 2 clinic
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 5 and Appendix O; IEI301 Integrated Transaction Project Brief and milestone worksheets
Before class: compare Appendices N and O. In class: decide distributor versus representative. After class: submit Milestone 2 contract/channel outputs.

UNIT 5. TRANSPORTATION, FREIGHT FORWARDING, AND CARGO RISK
5.1 Transport mode and route selection
- Product characteristics, lead time, cost, reliability, capacity, security, and sustainability
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapters 6 and 9; mode-selection worksheet
Before class: review mode characteristics. In class: select a mode and route for contrasting cargo cases. After class: prepare a route rationale for the project.
5.2 Ocean transportation, cargo forms, vessels, containerization, and bill-of-lading context
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 9; selected figures and cases
Before class: review ocean-cargo forms. In class: match cargo, vessel, service, and document type. After class: identify operational and documentary risks.
5.3 Air, road, rail, and multimodal transportation; freight forwarders and NVOCCs
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 9; intermediary-comparison worksheet
Before class: review non-ocean modes and intermediary roles. In class: design a multimodal chain and select service providers. After class: document handover points and accountability.

5.4 Freight calculation and transport quotation workshop
- Weight/measurement, chargeable basis, FCL/LCL considerations, and comparison of alternatives
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 9 and Appendix J; freight worksheet
Before class: review freight-calculation examples. In class: calculate and compare freight alternatives. After class: update project costing and route assumptions.
5.5 Cargo risks, loss prevention, carrier liability, and evidence preservation
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapters 6 and 9; cargo-risk register
Before class: identify cargo-specific hazards. In class: build a risk-control plan. After class: specify preventive controls and evidence required if loss occurs.

5.6 Marine and air cargo insurance
- Insurable interest, ICC coverage logic, total/partial loss, general average, and insurance selection
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 6; insurance-comparison tables and general-average example
Before class: compare coverage levels. In class: select insurance and calculate a general-average contribution. After class: justify coverage and insured value.

UNIT 6. INSURANCE CLAIMS AND TRADE DOCUMENTS
6.1 Cargo claims, notice, survey, mitigation, settlement, and subrogation
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 6; cargo-claim checklist
Before class: review claim steps. In class: assemble and sequence a claim file. After class: draft preliminary notice and a claim-evidence checklist.

6.2 Trade-document architecture and functions
- Commercial, transport, insurance, payment, origin, inspection, and customs documents
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 9 and Appendix P; document-purpose matrix
Before class: review sample documents. In class: map issuer, signer, recipient, purpose, and data dependencies. After class: complete the document architecture for the project.

6.3 Progress Test 2 and applied debrief
- Scope: Units 3–5 and foundational insurance/document concepts
Assigned materials from Sessions 10–29; review guide
Complete the individual closed-book Progress Test 2. After the test: diagnose one calculation, contract, logistics, or insurance misconception.

6.4 Commercial invoice, pro forma invoice, packing list, and purchase order
- Required fields, value/quantity logic, and documentary alignment
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 9 and Appendix P; document templates
Before class: inspect sample forms. In class: prepare and cross-check documents. After class: revise project documents and record changes.

6.5 Transport documents
- Ocean B/L, AWB, inland/through B/L, negotiability, clean/claused status, consignee, notify party, and shipment evidence
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 9; transport-document cases
Before class: compare B/L and AWB functions. In class: interpret document fields and identify defects. After class: specify the correct transport-document requirements for the project.

6.6 Certificate of origin, insurance certificate, inspection certificate, bill of exchange, and cross-document consistency audit
- Project document-pack checkpoint
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapters 9 and 18; Appendix P; IEI301 Integrated Transaction Project Brief and milestone worksheets
Before class: assemble the current project documents. In class: conduct a full consistency audit. After class: submit the corrected document-pack checkpoint and discrepancy log.

UNIT 7. FOREIGN-EXCHANGE RISK, INTERNATIONAL PAYMENT, AND TRADE FINANCE
7.1 Exchange-rate quotation, transaction exposure, contract currency, and simple hedging
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 10; FX worksheet
Before class: review direct/indirect quotations. In class: calculate exposure and compare hedged/unhedged outcomes. After class: recommend a contract currency and control.

7.2 Payment-method risk spectrum
- Cash in advance, open account, consignment, credit insurance, and negotiation of payment terms
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 11; payment-risk matrix
Before class: compare payment risks. In class: negotiate seller/buyer positions. After class: justify a payment method for the project.

7.3 Documentary collection
- Parties, collection instruction, D/P, D/A, bank roles, refusal, and URC 522
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 11; URC 522 reference; collection-flow worksheet
Before class: review the collection flow. In class: simulate D/P and D/A. After class: prepare a collection instruction and contingency response.

7.4 Documentary credits
- Applicant, beneficiary, issuing/advising/confirming banks, credit flow, independence principle, and UCP 600
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 11; UCP 600 reference; L/C flow diagram
Before class: review parties and flows. In class: map goods, documents, and money. After class: specify L/C requirements for the project.

- Classification, correction, waiver, presentation risk, and bank dishonour
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 11; Appendix P L/C requirements; discrepancy checklist
Before class: review discrepancy examples. In class: examine a document set against an L/C. After class: prepare a discrepancy report and corrective plan.
7.6 Documentary fraud, collusion, authenticity, and protective controls
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 11 closing cases; fraud-red-flag worksheet
Before class: review fraud cases. In class: identify red flags and control failures. After class: design seller, buyer, and bank control measures.

7.7 Special credits and guarantees

Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapter 11; special-credit comparison worksheet
Before class: review special instruments. In class: match instruments to transaction needs. After class: justify whether any special credit or guarantee is required.

7.8 Trade finance
- Factoring, forfaiting, buyer/supplier credit, receivables finance, export credit insurance, and ECA support
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapters 13–14; finance-selection worksheet
Before class: compare financing methods. In class: select finance for short-, medium-, and long-term cases. After class: evaluate cost, recourse, maturity, and risk.

7.9 Integrated payment and finance decision laboratory
- FX, payment, document, credit, and cash-flow coherence
- Project Milestone 3 clinic
Seyoum (2022), Export–Import Theory, Practices, and Procedures, 4th ed.: Chapters 10–14; IEI301 Integrated Transaction Project Brief and milestone worksheets
Before class: bring contract, payment, and finance assumptions. In class: stress-test the transaction. After class: submit Milestone 3 payment/finance outputs.

UNIT 8. EXPORT–IMPORT COMPLIANCE, ETHICS, IPR, AND DIGITAL TRADE

Before class: review origin concepts. In class: assess preferential eligibility. After class: specify the origin evidence and unresolved verification risks.

Before class: assemble tariff, value, origin, and tax inputs. In class: calculate duty/tax and audit customs readiness. After class: submit the project customs/compliance checkpoint.

UNIT 10. TRADE REMEDIES, ALTERNATIVE TRANSACTIONS, AND COURSE INTEGRATION
